children.text: Magikland is an open-air theme park of about 5 hectares in Silay City, north of Bacolod, billed as the first theme park in the Visayas. Themed on the Negros legend of the Bakunawa, the moon-eating dragon, it has 12 rides and a Cultural Zone that recreates Silay's old mansions, and it opens only on Friday to Sunday afternoons.

Magikland is an open-air theme park in Sitio Cabug, Barangay Guinhalaran, Silay City, Negros Occidental. Its operator, Aton Land and Leisure, built it on a site of about 5 hectares, and both the park's own description and Wikipedia call it the first outdoor theme park in the Visayas and a park made and inspired by Negrenses. Ground was broken in April 2017 and the park had its soft opening on September 27, 2019; Wikipedia cites a report that puts the total cost at 800 million pesos. It halted operations in 2020 because of COVID-19 and reopened on November 14 of that year under health protocols.

The park's theme is Negros folklore. Its main character is the Bakunawa, the dragon known for swallowing the moon, joined by four child-warrior characters who stand against it. This world is tied to the film Magikland (directed by Peque Gallaga), which was entered in the 2020 Metro Manila Film Festival. That gives the park the feel of walking through a storybook town rather than an ordinary amusement park, and children enjoy it more if you tell them about the characters.

The park has three zones. The Magical Zone has gentle rides for children, the Mystical Zone has thrill rides, and the Cultural Zone has photo spots styled after Silay's old mansions plus a Ferris wheel. There are 12 rides in all, and Coasterpedia lists many of them as Italian-made Zamperla models. If you expect a big roller coaster or dozens of rides you may be disappointed; the size suits a family looking for a light half-day outing.

The key thing to know before you go is the operating schedule. According to the official information, the park is open only on Friday, Saturday and Sunday from 1 PM to 8 PM and closed Monday to Thursday. If you are staying in Bacolod on weekdays and make a special trip, you may find it closed, so plan it for a weekend. Holiday and event periods have their own schedules, and monthly schedules are posted on the official website and Facebook page. For travelers, Magikland's appeal is that it is close and low-pressure. It is near Bacolod-Silay Airport, and Silay itself has historic old mansions and a cathedral, so a morning in Silay town followed by an afternoon at Magikland works well. On the other hand, it is more accurate to tell anyone expecting a large, ride-focused theme park that this one is small.
The Silay Eye in the Cultural Zone is a Ferris wheel about
tall. Wikipedia says it offers views over Silay City. Ride it around sunset to see the park lights and the surrounding fields together, so time your visit for late afternoon.

Crazy Trail in the Mystical Zone is a spinning wild-mouse-style ride that Coasterpedia classes as the park's only roller coaster. It is not large, but its sharp turns make it popular with children and teenagers. The official website does not list a height limit, so ask at the entrance.

The Sky Tower is a drop tower that lifts riders up and then drops them, and Disk'O and the Family Swinger are also in the Mystical Zone. All are for thrill seekers, so if you are prone to motion sickness, try one and decide how to continue based on how you feel.

blocks.title: Gentle rides in the children's zone

children.text: The Magical Zone has Crazy Surf, Magic Bike, Smasher bumper cars, Happy Swing, Mt. Kanlaon and the Magikland Express. Mt. Kanlaon is described as a children's ride. Families with toddlers will find waits shorter and the rides safer if they stay mostly in this zone.

The Fantasy Carousel in the Cultural Zone is a carousel the whole family can ride together. It also photographs well, so it is a popular spot for parents and children to take a souvenir picture together.

blocks.title: Photo spot styled after Silay's old mansions

children.text: The Cultural Zone has an area themed on Silay's heritage and is described as a good place for photos. Silay is a city known for old mansions built by sugar barons, so this area also works as a preview of the atmosphere before you see the mansions in town.

The official website says the Mariit Mansion is open every Saturday. During the Halloween event from late October to early November 2026, the mansion experience was offered along with a Zombie Run, a Monster Parade and stage shows. How to join and what it costs differ by period, so check the official announcement.

A 2021 SunStar report mentions midway games such as ring toss, archery and basketball, and a playground called Butantanding. Check on site whether the same facilities are still running. They are a good way for children to pass the time while waiting for rides.

items.title: Half-day family route
items.subtitle: A relaxed visit timed to the 1 PM opening

children.text: Buy your tickets at the entrance ticket booth when the park opens. The official website recommends buying online in advance to avoid the queue.
Start with the Magical Zone. Crazy Surf, Magic Bike and the bumper cars let the children warm up first.
Ride Crazy Trail, Sky Tower and Disk'O in the Mystical Zone. If the midday heat is strong, rest in the shade first.
Take photos in front of the old-mansion scenery in the Cultural Zone and ride the Fantasy Carousel.
Ride the Silay Eye Ferris wheel around sunset. This is when the photos look best and the temperature drops.
About 30 minutes before closing, head toward the exit and arrange your ride home.
The park runs Friday to Sunday from
to
, so this route is possible only on weekends. Public transport is scarce at night, so decide how you will get back in advance.

items.title: Full-day Silay route
items.subtitle: Town in the morning, Magikland in the afternoon

children.text: Look around Silay town's old mansions and cathedral. San Diego Pro-Cathedral, Silay is close by.
Have lunch in town.
Go to Magikland by tricycle or taxi and enter.
Use the all-access pass to ride the rides zone by zone.
Finish with a ride on the Ferris wheel.
Closing days and visiting hours differ from one town mansion to another. Check before you go.
Take a direct flight from Manila (NAIA) to Bacolod-Silay Airport (BCD). The flight time is known to be roughly
1 hour 10 minutes–1 hour 25 minutes
, so check the airline's latest schedule.
The official website says you can get from the airport to the park by tricycle from the main gate or by taxi from the arrival area.
Take a jeepney toward Silay from the Bacolod North Terminal and get off at the Bangga Carmela junction, as the official website advises.
From the junction it is about
1km
to the park, which you can walk or cover by pedicab or electric tricycle.
A taxi or Grab goes right up to the park. Distance and fare vary with time of day and traffic, so check locally.

The official website says to follow the Lacson Street highway from Bacolod and turn right at Bangga Carmela in Guinhalaran; the park is in front of Carmela Subdivision. Confirm the location with a navigation app.
From BREDCO Port or Banago Port, first head toward the North Terminal, then take a jeepney or bus bound for Guinhalaran. The last stretch is the same as above.

Because it is an outdoor park, avoiding rainy days matters most. In general, the dry season from November to May is the comfortable time to ride. Since the park opens at 1 PM and midday heat is strong from March to May, late afternoon through the evening is the pleasant time then.

During the rainy season from June to October, showers can stop rides. If a typhoon approaches the park may close, so check the official Facebook announcements. On weekend afternoons family crowds can make lines long for popular rides.

The menus and prices of restaurants and stalls inside the park are not on the official website, so I could not confirm them. Because the park opens at 1 PM, it is safer to have lunch in Silay town or Bacolod first. Ask at the entrance whether you may bring in water and snacks.

There is no lodging inside the park. As it is close to the airport, you can stay in Bacolod and make a trip, or use a small guesthouse in Silay town. Combining The Ruins in Bacolod with Silay's old quarter makes for a full day.
The park is open only Friday, Saturday and Sunday from
to
, so do not plan a visit for Monday to Thursday.
The official website recommends buying tickets online to skip the line. General entry needs no reservation.
If you plan to ride only two or three rides, compare the ₱280 general admission plus individual ride prices; if you plan to ride a lot, compare it with the ₱650 all-access pass and choose.
The official website lists no height or age limits for the rides, so if you bring young children, ask at the ticket booth first.
Monthly operating schedules are posted as images. Check the latest announcements on the official website and Facebook before you go.
There is little shade by day, so bring a hat, sunscreen and water; after sunset it turns cooler, so a light jacket is handy.
For inquiries, use the official number 0998 565 6530 or email. Contact them in advance for events and group bookings.
Transport can be scarce at night, so decide before closing how you will call a taxi or Grab.
The park is open only on Friday to Sunday afternoons and the monthly schedule changes. Be sure to check the official announcement before you visit.
The official website states that prices and hours can change without notice. The values here reflect what was checked in November 2026.
Rain or typhoons can stop rides or close the park.
Do not ride thrill rides if you have heart or back conditions or are pregnant. Follow the instructions of the staff on site.
Keep valuables on your person and watch your belongings in the crowded weekend lines.
Agree on the fare before getting into a taxi or tricycle, and check whether ride-hailing apps are available.
A city of old mansions and a cathedral a short drive from the park. It is a good place to explore in the morning.

Bacolod city and The Ruins are easy to combine with Magikland in a one-day itinerary. Distance and travel time vary with traffic, so check locally.
